title: "Quiz 3"
author: "Helen Girma"
date: "2026-11-15"
output: html_document
---
1. Load the spotify dataset (available in github repository).
```{r}
library(readr)
spotify <- read_csv("spotifyDat Fall26.csv")
```

2. Create a bar graph of the artist column (Hint: use theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90)) to rotate the x axis).
```{r}

library(tidyverse)
ggplot(spotify, aes(artist)) + geom_bar() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90))
```

3. Add genre as a third variable in your graph.
```{r}
ggplot(spotify, aes(artist, fill = as.factor(genre))) + geom_bar() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90))

ggplot(spotify, aes(artist, fill = genre)) + geom_bar() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90))

```

4. Use color brewer to add color to your graph in 3. 
```{r}
ggplot(spotify, aes(artist, fill = as.factor(genre))) + geom_bar() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90))+scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Blues")

#Blues only has 9 colors available, which is why several genres are not colored
```

5. Place the legend for the graph you made in 3 on the bottom of the graph. 
```{r}
ggplot(spotify, aes(artist, fill = as.factor(genre))) + geom_bar() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90), legend.position = "bottom")

```

As you probably recognized, the graph you made is really hard to read.

6. Separate the genre column into multiple columns (e.g. so each genre listed is in a unique column)
```{r}
spotifyGenre <- spotify %>% separate(genre, into = c("genre1", "genre2", "genre3"), sep = ",")
```

7. Use these genre columns to create a dataset in long format. 
```{r}
spotifyLong <- pivot_longer(spotifyGenre, cols = c("genre1", "genre2", "genre3"), names_to = "genreNum", values_to = "genre", values_drop_na = TRUE)

```

8.use facet wrap to make graphs of artist by genre 
```{r}
ggplot(spotifyLong, aes(artist))+geom_bar()+facet_wrap(~genre) + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90))
```

9. Create a graph that includes the variables tempo and dancability. 
```{r}
ggplot(spotify, aes(danceability, tempo))+ geom_point()
```

10. Add popularity as a third variable. 
```{r}
ggplot(spotify, aes(tempo, danceability, color = popularity))+ geom_point()

```

11. Use viridis as a color in your graph from #10
```{r}
library(viridis)

ggplot(spotify, aes(tempo, danceability, color = popularity))+ geom_point() + scale_color_viridis(option = "magma", direction = -1) + theme_classic() + xlab("Tempo")+ylab("Danceability")+ggtitle("Tempo Compared to Danceability of Spotify Songs")

```
